Blind consumer A-2: one digest, three admitted textual forms. plan.nativeContextDigests takes the bare 64 hex; a native record field typed Sha256Text takes `sha256:`+hex; a foundation identity takes its typed prefix.

A matching nativeContextId commits to the CONTEXT bytes, not to the universe's copy of them. Every field the two records both carry, and every universe flag that is a function of context bytes, must agree; five contradictions are checked here.
The row set is the COMPLETE declaration inventory of the retained tree, selected or not; otherwise two different standard libraries could mint one context.
The component join is by basename, so an ambiguous tree is refused rather than resolved arbitrarily.

The context carries no platform FIELD because TypeScript resolution semantics are platform-invariant by design; the identity is not, because toolClosure.closureId names a closure whose foundation descriptor includes `platform`. nodeModulesLayoutDigest that is not the digest of the retained layout is refused.
nodeModulesInReadSet is not a free flag: it is exactly whether the context retains a layout. The false branch stays available and means every bare specifier is an unresolved edge.
Exactly as for the Rust binding: an optional retained-input check is not a rule.
A universe naming a program root the analysed snapshot does not contain is refused.

An extends edge to a config the graph does not retain is refused.
Every retained node must be reachable from the selected entry; a stray config is not read.
The entry cannot be relabelled: kind is checked against the basename.
A selected entry the graph does not retain is refused rather than defaulted.
configOrigin synthesized means no config file was read; nodes contradict that.

cases.note: CB6-MUST-2. `kind` is inside C(TypeScriptConfigGraphV1) and therefore inside tsconfigGraphHash, the universe identity and the RunId, but the prose delegated it to "the schema and native admission" and neither stated it. The derivation is now published at native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-config-node-kind-law and READ by the model. Every row here is a path two conforming readings could disagree on: the widespread tsconfig*.json PREFIX convention would call tsconfig.build.json, tsconfig.base.json and tsconfig.jsonc `tsconfig` and mint a different RunId for the same repository. Non-entry depth and case are covered too - the rule is the exact, case-sensitive basename and nothing else.
The model does not restate the table: it reads #/x-opensip-config-node-kind-law. This pins the two together so a change to either without the other fails here rather than silently moving an identity.

The prefix reading applied to a base of the entry. This node derives NOTHING - configOrigin reads only the entry - yet it is committed to tsconfigGraphHash, so an unpublished rule left two RunIds available for one repository. It refuses.

A host that lowercases the basename before comparing - natural on a case-insensitive filesystem - produces a different graph and a different identity. The comparison is case-SENSITIVE and TSConfig.json is `other`; claiming tsconfig refuses. Its configOrigin is still tsconfig, because an `other` ENTRY is a selected custom-named configuration.

Why this is a MUST and not a wording preference: the exact-basename reading and the prefix reading of the SAME repository produce two different tsconfigGraphHash values, which the universe requires, and the universe identity reaches fact2/scope2/coverage2/view2/evidence3/seal3/run3. Both digests are computed here from the same nodes differing only in the kind of tsconfig.build.json. The prefix graph is schema-valid and REFUSED by admission - which is exactly what the published law buys: without it, nothing compared the value to anything. The historical evaluator2 graph reached evidence2/seal2/run2; that is the historical counterexample, not a current qualified claim.

CB6-ADV-1. Section 1.2 selects a MODE inside a unit; it does not discover one. Read alone, the js-synthesized recognition cell ("package.json present OR any .js file under the unit") looked like an independent test and would have minted a unit for a directory of bare .js files, changing membership and therefore the Plan. U-1 governs: with no tsconfig.json, no jsconfig.json and no package.json there is no tsjs unit for a .js file to be "under", and each such file is syntax-only / no-program-unit-for-language rather than a program member.

The positive half of the same boundary, so the clarification is not read as removing the mode: add the U-1 marker and the identical files become program members of one js-synthesized unit. The marker makes the unit; the .js files never did.

CB6-ADV-2. The scope of section 4.8's second clause. It is NOT narrowed to types@checked - that reading would be a WEAKENING, permitting a native clones or references provider to emit a fabricated percentage, which is exactly what 4.8 removed. It is a provider-emission law over the bundle: TypeDerivationV1 pins confidenceMillionths to the constant 1000000 and is the only record carrying confidenceMethod. Section 4.6 step 3 stays reachable because it compares ViewEntryV3.confidenceMillionths, whose domain is deliberately the wider 0..1000000 and which carries NO method, so an imported, non-native or defective contribution is still judged. The named regression fixture at 100000 is a hand-built EVALUATOR input, not a ViewEntryV3 and not provider emission - it fails ViewEntryV3 admission here - so it is no counterexample to the emission law and this contract claims no product emission of such a value.

Two rows for ONE (capabilityId, languageMode, workspaceRoot) disagreeing only on `required`. uniqueItems sees two DISTINCT items and admits them, and the per-row vocabulary loop judges each alone, so nothing refused this before; both rows enter analysisSpecDigest and therefore PlanId, so the undetermined requiredness is COMMITTED.
The SAME law at the analysis-spec boundary. admit_requested_capabilities is the helper BOTH this boundary and retained Run closure call, so the two agree by construction.
Only the tuple is constrained. A different unit root is a different cell.
DIAGNOSTIC PRECEDENCE. Two rows cannot contend for ownership of a cell that is not a registered cell at all, so the vocabulary keeps its own more specific refusal.
The existing external-configuration / externally-supplied-spec / host-generated routes carry the refusal; no public DomainDetailCode member is added.
A kind=failure CommandEnvelope requires a NONEMPTY errors array even where the termination lawfully carries no detail.

The exact reproduced vector: two DISTINCT ScopeDocumentV1 payloads under the ONE registered document digest. The registry refused two REGISTRY ROWS for one digest (PAYLOAD_PARAMETER_AMBIGUOUS_ROW) and never constrained two SPEC ENTRIES citing one row. The digests are re-derived in the first three steps so this case cannot drift from the documents it names.
An ordinary analysis that needs no scope-policy input selects none. No default is invented and the foundation scope-descriptor never substitutes.

A host may examine the committed partition exhaustively and still answer `unknown` because the evidence it needs is MISSING rather than unexamined - ambiguous or missing Rust compilation ownership, an undeclared or unservable capability, an unlisted source variant. Banning that pair would force a host to understate its own examination to report an honest unknown.
RC-3: coverage=complete beside resolutionCompleteness.state=incomplete over real unresolved edges is the EXPECTED result for most JavaScript and non-prepared Rust, and stays lawful.
They read different things and both report: RC-6 the examination claim, RC-2 the resolution claim.
